message.content:
Sure! Here are a few kitchen appliances that can bake a chocolate cake:

| Machine | Why it’s good for baking a chocolate cake | Typical use |
|---------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|
| **Conventional oven** | Provides even heat and can reach the high temperatures (350–375 °F / 175–190 °C) needed for a classic cake. | Most home bakers use this for reliable results. |
| **Convection oven** | Uses a fan to circulate hot air, which can bake cakes slightly faster and more evenly. | Great if you want a crisp top and consistent rise. |
| **Toaster oven** | Compact and convenient for small batches; many models have a bake setting that works well for a single-layer cake. | Ideal for quick, single-serving cakes or when you don’t have a full-size oven. |
| **Microwave oven** | With a microwave-safe cake pan and a “cake” or “bake” setting, you can make a quick mug cake or a small sheet cake. | Perfect for a fast, single-serving treat. |
| **Electric oven** | Similar to a conventional oven but often more energy‑efficient and easier to control temperature. | Common in many households. |
| **Smart oven** | Offers programmable settings, Wi‑Fi connectivity, and sometimes pre‑set recipes for cakes. | Good for tech‑savvy bakers who want precise control. |
| **Cake maker / bread machine** | Some models have a “cake” setting that mixes batter and bakes it automatically. | Convenient for beginners or those who want a hands‑off experience. |

**Tip:** If you’re baking a chocolate cake for the first time, a conventional or convection oven is usually the safest bet. Just preheat to 350 °F (175 °C), grease your pan, and follow your favorite chocolate cake recipe. Happy baking!
